assessment.nobel_worthiness: Predicting and then observing topological insulators opened a whole class of matter protected by symmetry and band topology. The Kane-Mele theory and the HgTe edge-state transport are conceptually clean and have shaped a wide field well beyond the original systems. From a theory-of-complex-systems view this is a durable, general organizing principle.
assessment.attribution: Kane and Mele made the decisive theoretical proposal (quantum spin Hall effect, Z2 invariant). Molenkamp's group delivered the first experimental realization in HgTe wells (with Bernevig-Hughes-Zhang theory, not credited here). M. Zahid Hasan's 3D photoemission work is also important, so the three-person limit forces a choice. I propose Kane, Mele and Molenkamp as the theory-plus-experiment core.
assessment.maturity: Confirmed independently across many materials and platforms for nearly two decades; interpretation is stable. Timing is mature, and the 2016 prize recognized topological phase transitions but not this discovery.
uncertainties: Whether Hasan, or the Bernevig-Hughes-Zhang proposal (not on this list), should displace one of the credited names.
The 2D versus 3D split may make the compound discovery hard to fit into one prize.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The magic-angle flat-band prediction and the observation of correlated insulation and superconductivity in twisted bilayer graphene created moire quantum matter as a tunable many-body platform. Originality is high and the impact on correlated-electron physics is already very large.
assessment.attribution: Bistritzer and MacDonald supplied the continuum-model prediction of flat bands at the magic angle; Jarillo-Herrero's group made the decisive experimental discovery. This is a natural theory-plus-experiment trio on the supplied credit, though Cao and others in the experiments are not available to name.
assessment.maturity: Reproduced by many groups, but the nature of the superconductivity and the correlated states is still debated. Recognition may be somewhat early, yet the core discovery is solid.
uncertainties: Pairing mechanism and phase diagram are unsettled.
Individual experimental contributors beyond Jarillo-Herrero are not on the credited list.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Optical lattice clocks, built on the magic-wavelength idea, reached fractional uncertainties near 1e-18 and enable tests of fundamental physics, geodesy and a possible redefinition of the second. The concept is original and the practical impact is large.
assessment.attribution: Katori proposed the magic-wavelength optical lattice clock and first realized it; Ye's group pushed it to record precision and many-body (Fermi-degenerate) regimes. A two-person award fits the supplied credit well. Other clock groups are not credited, so I note but do not assume further claims.
assessment.maturity: Strongly confirmed by multiple national laboratories; progress is continuing but the concept itself is mature. Timely.
uncertainties: Competing contributions from ion-clock and other lattice-clock groups may complicate allocation.
Ye already shares the 2005-era frequency-comb community context; I rely on memory for that and have not verified it.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Ultracold atoms in optical lattices realized the Hubbard model with controlled parameters, giving access to Mott insulators, magnetism and out-of-equilibrium many-body dynamics, and enabling single-site microscopy. This connects directly to statistical-physics questions about interacting many-body systems and is broadly influential.
assessment.attribution: Zoller and Cirac (with Jaksch et al.) proposed the Hubbard-model realization and quantum simulation concept; Bloch's group delivered the decisive experiments (Mott transition, quantum gas microscopy). Greiner and Esslinger also made core experimental contributions, so five names compete for three slots. I choose the theory pair plus Bloch.
assessment.maturity: Well established and reproduced widely over two decades; the simulation of fermionic Hubbard physics at low temperature is still progressing, but the core claim is mature.
uncertainties: Allocation among Bloch, Greiner and Esslinger is contestable.
Overlap with B041 and with the 2012 prize for quantum control of single particles.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The observation of a diffuse flux of high-energy astrophysical neutrinos, and later the association with the blazar TXS 0506+056 and the Galactic plane, opened neutrino astronomy at PeV energies. The instrumental achievement of a cubic-kilometre ice detector is original and the result is clear.
assessment.attribution: Halzen was the principal driver of the IceCube concept and its science case; Karle and Spiering held key leadership and development roles in AMANDA and IceCube. A very large collaboration makes individual attribution delicate, and I cannot independently verify the detailed roles.
assessment.maturity: The diffuse flux is confirmed in several channels; source identification is still limited to a few cases. Timing is reasonable but source physics is incomplete.
uncertainties: Collaboration-scale credit and the role of other leaders (such as AMANDA founders) is not captured by three names.
Source origin of most neutrinos remains unknown.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Circuit quantum electrodynamics provides strong coupling between superconducting qubits and microwave resonators and underlies readout, coupling and control in leading quantum processors. The idea is original and technologically consequential.
assessment.attribution: Blais and collaborators proposed the cQED architecture in 2004; Wallraff and Schoelkopf demonstrated strong coupling and led the development of the transmon-based platform. The supplied trio matches this proposal-plus-experiment split.
assessment.maturity: Mature and universally adopted. Its proximity to the 2025 prize on macroscopic quantum tunnelling in circuits may affect timing, a point I note without having verified the full details.
uncertainties: Relation to recent recognition of superconducting-circuit work may reduce priority.
Contributions of the transmon inventors (Koch, Schoelkopf, Devoret) are only partly captured.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The jamming picture unified the rigidity transition of granular matter, foams and glasses as a critical point with scaling and a diverging length scale. It is a conceptual contribution of the kind I value in complex systems, bringing universality ideas to athermal disordered matter.
assessment.attribution: Liu and Nagel proposed and developed the jamming phase diagram; O'Hern, Silbert, Durian and Witten also contributed key numerics and theory, which are not credited here. A two-person prize is feasible but contested.
assessment.maturity: Strongly supported by simulations and experiments, although the exact universality class and the relation to the glass transition remain under discussion. Less decisively confirmed than the experimental candidates above.
uncertainties: Missing co-contributors on the numerical and theoretical side.
Open question about whether jamming is truly a critical phenomenon in experiments.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Cavity optomechanics brought mechanical oscillators to their quantum ground state, with sideband cooling, strong coupling and quantum-limited measurement, and connects to gravitational-wave detection and quantum sensing. The field is original and conceptually clear.
assessment.attribution: Aspelmeyer, Kippenberg and Painter each made central contributions (radiation-pressure cooling, strong coupling, ground-state cooling and nanophotonic devices); the supplied trio is reasonable, though Teufel, Lehnert and others also reached the ground state.
assessment.maturity: The quantum regime is confirmed by several independent groups and platforms. Applications beyond metrology are still developing, so recognition may still be somewhat early.
uncertainties: Competing credit for ground-state cooling (electromechanical systems) is not captured.
Distinct from LIGO-related squeezing recognition, with some overlap of ideas.
